articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del Sevilla vs Osasuna, que se juega este lunes 26 de octubre en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, correspondiente a la décima jornada de LaLiga 26/27
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del Sevilla vs Osasuna, que se juega este lunes 26 de octubre en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, correspondiente a la décima jornada de LaLiga 26/27
articles.body: El conjunto hispalense llega en la parte alta de la tabla, sexto tras nueve jornadas con 14 puntos. El Osasuna, con 11, vive un momento de transición, con el regreso de Jagoba Arrasate al banquillo, y busca romper su mala dinámica lejos de casa. Favorito para el partido entre Sevilla y Osasuna Con estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Sevilla, aunque sin una diferencia demasiado amplia. Codere paga su victoria a cuota 1.90, una cifra moderada que refleja que los locales parten por delante, pero sin demasiado margen. El Osasuna llega con la moral reforzada tras vencer 2-0 al Racing de Santander en el estreno de Arrasate. Ante un rival que ha marcado diez goles en nueve partidos, su triunfo en Sevilla se paga a 4.00. Ante Budimir, con siete goles en Liga, el Sevilla tendrá que cuidar mucho su área. El empate, a cuota 3.40, cobra relevancia en un cruce igualado, en el que los precedentes recientes reparten los puntos con frecuencia. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes de las apuestas deportivas. El Sevilla ha encajado 16 goles en nueve jornadas y llega con varias bajas en su plantilla, entre ellas Marcão, Guridi y Sierra, además de la duda de Kochorashvili. Con estos datos, Codere paga el Sí a 1.92, una cuota atractiva para un equipo local que no termina de cerrar su defensa. Por otro lado, el Osasuna ha encajado 18 tantos, pero ha firmado solo diez a favor, lo que demuestra que no siempre encuentra la portería. Si el Sevilla se adelanta y gestiona bien el partido, el No gana peso y se paga a 1.8. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con presencia de tantos. En lo que va de Liga, los partidos del Sevilla acumulan más de tres goles de media, y los del Osasuna rondan esa cifra. Ninguno de los dos aparece como un bloque sólido en defensa. Por eso, la línea de 2.5 goles resulta asequible para el Over, que cotiza a 2.10 en Codere. No obstante, la llegada de Arrasate puede traducirse en un Osasuna más ordenado y compacto, algo que le llevaría a jugar con el partido controlado y pocas ocasiones. En ese escenario, un 1-0 o un 1-1 dejaría el marcador por debajo. El Under 2.5 se paga a 1.65. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Sevilla juega en casa con la intención de buscar amplitud por las bandas, con jugadores como Félix Correia y Rubén Vargas, lo que suele generar saques de esquina si el rival se encierra. El Osasuna, por su parte, podría adoptar una actitud compacta durante largos tramos, lo que favorecería un buen volumen de córners para los locales.

articles.title: Rusia volverá a ser sede del Mundial de un deporte olímpico más de ocho años después
articles.standfirst: Desde febrero de 2022, cuando comenzó la guerra en Ucrania, Rusia ha estado proscrita por las federaciones internacionales
articles.summary: Desde febrero de 2022, cuando comenzó la guerra en Ucrania, Rusia ha estado proscrita por las federaciones internacionales
articles.body: El Kremlin celebró este lunes la decisión de la Federación Internacional de Halterofilia (IWF) de celebrar el Campeonato Mundial de 2030 en Moscú. "Rusia debe retornar de pleno derecho a la familia deportiva mundial, porque esta familia no puede vivir plenamente sin la participación rusa", aseveró durante su rueda de prensa telefónica diaria el portavoz de la Presidencia rusa, Dmitri Peskov. La IWF anunció este domingo que la capital rusa será sede del Mundial de 2030, decisión que marca un nuevo paso hacia el retorno de Rusia al calendario de las grandes competencias internacionales. Será el primer Mundial de un deporte del programa olímpico que se celebrará en Rusia desde febrero de 2022, cuando comenzó la guerra en Ucrania. La decisión fue adoptada por el Comité Ejecutivo de la IWF, que confirmó que Ahmedabad, en India, recibirá el Mundial de 2029, y asignó los Mundiales juveniles de 2028 a Pristina, en Kosovo, y los juveniles Sub 20 a Caracas, Venezuela A la vez, en respuesta a la posibilidad de que Rusia acoja unos Juegos Olímpicos en un futuro, Peskov llamó a "no adelantarse a los acontecimientos". "Ahora en realidad no son muchos los países que se muestran interesados en convertirse en sedes de Juegos Olímpicos. Es necesario equilibrarlo todo, las cosas a favor y en contra de las decisiones correspondientes. De momento, el asunto no está en el orden del día", indicó. Rusia fue siempre sede habitual de grandes campeonatos y en los últimos años, antes de atacar Ucrania, había organizado hasta una Copa del Mundo de fútbol en 2018.

articles.title: NHL Trade Rumors: Dylan Larkin deal could be closer than expected as Red Wings face critical days
articles.summary: NHL trade rumors around Dylan Larkin have reached a potentially important stretch, with a prediction pointing to late October as a possible window for a
articles.body: NHL trade rumors around Dylan Larkin have reached a potentially important stretch, with a prediction pointing to late October as a possible window for a deal. Detroit has reportedly explored young centers around the league, while Larkin has widened the list of teams he would consider joining. Those developments have added urgency to a story that has lingered for months, but they are not proof that a trade is close. The Red Wings still need an offer that meets their expectations, and Larkin must approve any destination because of his full no-trade clause.NHL trade rumors put Dylan Larkin in focusOn October 16, analyst John Buccigross said on Frankly Hockey that he expected a Detroit trade within seven to 10 days. When Frank Seravalli asked if he meant Larkin rather than defenseman Simon Edvinsson, Buccigross confirmed Larkin was the player he had in mind. That forecast placed the possible window around October 23-26.On October 22, NHL insider Elliotte Friedman reported that the Red Wings had asked other teams about young centers, including prospects who have yet to play in the NHL. Friedman could not confirm whether those conversations involved Larkin, Edvinsson or both. The discussions point to broader roster planning, not a confirmed trade plan.Larkin has also reportedly expanded his list of acceptable destinations from three teams to 10. The clubs named in reports include Colorado, Minnesota, New Jersey, Dallas, Washington, Carolina, Tampa Bay, Florida, Vegas and Utah. A longer list could give Detroit more room to negotiate, though Larkin would still have to approve the team involved.Detroit’s asking price could decide the outcomeThe bigger obstacle may be what the Red Wings want in return. TSN’s Darren Dreger has reported that Detroit is seeking two high-end prospects, a top-nine NHL forward and a first-round pick. That is a steep package, even for a proven center who could strengthen a contender.Some possible destinations may struggle to meet that price. Colorado has been linked as a fit but faces questions over available assets and salary-cap space. New Jersey’s situation may have shifted after its reported Connor Hellebuyck trade, while Minnesota could have a limited offer to put together. These are potential complications, not signs that talks with any one club are close.Detroit has good reason not to move Larkin for a disappointing return. He is a top-line center, and accepting less than the club believes he is worth would weaken its position. But a high asking price can also narrow the market if interested teams cannot assemble the right mix of players and picks.The late-October prediction may prove accurate, but it is still a forecast. If those days pass without a deal, that would not automatically mean negotiations have collapsed. The key question is whether Detroit can find a return it likes and a destination Larkin will accept. Until both conditions are met, trade talk remains just that.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What happened when NHL linesman Travis Gawryletz accidentally struck Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby during the game against Nashville Predators
articles.summary: During a game against the Nashville Predators, NHL linesman Travis Gawryletz accidentally struck Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby, leading to a dramatic 3-2 overtime win. Despite the collision, Crosby continued to play and assisted in the tying goal before securing victory for his team.
articles.body: Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby was accidentally struck in the face by NHL linesman Travis Gawryletz during the first period of Pittsburgh’s game against the Nashville Predators on October 24. The unexpected contact knocked Crosby to the ice, but he was able to continue playing.The unusual incident became one of the game’s most talked-about moments. Crosby later assisted on Pittsburgh’s tying goal, and the Penguins completed a comeback with a 3-2 overtime victory at PPG Paints Arena.What happened when Travis Gawryletz made contact with Sidney Crosby?The collision occurred in the opening minutes of the first period as Crosby moved across the ice. Gawryletz was extending his arm to signal an onside play when his arm caught the Penguins captain in the face. The unexpected contact sent Crosby down to the ice.The incident appeared accidental rather than a deliberate action by the official. Crosby had been skating toward the play when the linesman moved his arm outward, leaving the captain caught by surprise.The brief collision stood out because it involved a player and an on-ice official rather than contact between opposing players, and it also happened early in a game that would eventually develop into a closely contested matchup between Pittsburgh and Nashville.Was Sidney Crosby injured after the accidental hit?Crosby did not appear to suffer a serious injury from the collision and continued participating in the game. Reports said he briefly stepped away from a faceoff to check on his face and speak with the linesman before returning to the action.There was no indication in the available reports that the incident forced Crosby to leave the game. His subsequent contribution to Pittsburgh’s comeback also showed that he remained involved in the contest.The moment drew attention because of the unexpected nature of the contact, but the game continued without a reported extended stoppage related to the collision. The incident was not described as a deliberate hit or a disciplinary play.How did Sidney Crosby help Pittsburgh Penguins beat Nashville?Despite the unusual opening-period moment, Crosby played a role in Pittsburgh’s late comeback. With the Penguins trailing 2-1 in the third period, he delivered the pass that allowed Rickard Rakell to score the tying goal with 1:06 remaining in regulation. The assist was Crosby’s 1,111th with Pittsburgh, tying Hall of Fame defenseman Ray Bourque for the most assists with a single NHL franchise.Pittsburgh then completed the comeback in overtime. Ville Koivunen scored at 3:44 of the extra period to secure the 3-2 victory, giving the Penguins two points after they had trailed late in the game. Connor Dewar also scored for Pittsburgh, while Steven Stamkos and Jayden Struble found the net for Nashville.The result gave the Penguins consecutive wins after a four-game losing streak, adding significance to a night that featured both an unusual on-ice collision and a dramatic finish.Crosby’s response ensured the accidental contact did not define his performance. Rather, his assist on Rakell's tying goal and Pittsburgh's overtime victory became significant parts of the story of the game, and the collision with Gawryletz was a memorable and surprising moment of the NHL contest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor McDavid puts the NHL on notice as his latest Oilers run sparks a major conversation
articles.summary: Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid has reached a remarkable milestone by recording 31 points in his first 10 games of the 2026-27 NHL season, joining the ranks of Wayne Gretzky, Mike Bossy, and Mario Lemieux. In this article, we explore his record-breaking performance and what it means for the Oilers' season.
articles.body: Connor McDavid has joined Wayne Gretzky, Mike Bossy, and Mario Lemieux in an exclusive NHL scoring club after recording 31 points in his first 10 games of the 2026–27 season, and the Edmonton Oilers captain reached the milestone with a five-point performance in a 6–5 shootout victory over the Carolina Hurricanes on October 22.McDavid’s tally includes eight goals and 23 assists, making his start one of the most productive opening stretches in NHL history. The 29-year-old also surpassed Gretzky’s previous Edmonton franchise benchmark for points through the first 10 games of a season.Connor McDavid joins NHL legends after historic Edmonton Oilers startConnor McDavid became the fourth player in NHL history to record at least 30 points in the first 10 games of a season. He reached the milestone during Edmonton’s 6–5 shootout win over the Carolina Hurricanes, finishing the night with two goals and three assists.McDavid’s fifth point against Carolina came as he helped set up Leon Draisaitl’s power-play goal. He later scored again to tie the game at 5–5 with less than two minutes remaining in regulation, before Edmonton secured the victory in a shootout.The performance marked his third five-point game of the season. McDavid had previously recorded five points against the Vancouver Canucks on October 1 and the Utah Mammoth on October 17. His consistent production has helped him open the campaign with a point in each of Edmonton’s first 10 games.Which NHL legends achieved the milestone before McDavid?McDavid joins three legendary players who have hit 30 points in their first 10 games of a season in three different eras of NHL scoring.Wayne Gretzky: 30 points in 10 games for Edmonton Oilers in 1984-85.Mike Bossy: Also hit 30 points in the first 10 games of the 1984-85 season with the New York Islanders.Mario Lemieux: Did it three times with the Pittsburgh Penguins, in 1988-89, 1992-93 and 1995-96.Lemieux remains the standout in this category, having recorded 37 points through the first 10 games of the 1988–89 season, and McDavid’s 31-point total places him among the most prolific opening stretches in league history, although it does not surpass Lemieux’s mark.What does Connor McDavid’s historic NHL start mean for Edmonton?McDavid’s early production has given the Edmonton Oilers a major offensive boost. He is averaging 3.1 points per game, and that rate would translate to 260 points across an 84-game regular season if maintained. That figure is a projection, not a prediction, and sustaining such production over a full campaign would be an extraordinary challenge.Draisaitl, McDavid’s longtime teammate, praised the captain’s form after the Carolina game. According to NHL.com, Draisaitl described McDavid’s production as “just not real” and said it was a pleasure to share the ice with him. The comment reflected the remarkable level of performance McDavid has delivered early in the season.McDavid has also set a new Edmonton franchise benchmark for points through the first 10 games, moving beyond Gretzky’s previous mark of 30 in 1984–85. The milestone adds another chapter to his career with the Oilers, where he has played throughout his NHL career since being selected first overall in the 2015 draft.The immediate challenge is sustaining his production as opponents adjust their defensive plans, and McDavid’s speed, playmaking, and ability to create scoring opportunities have made him difficult to contain, but the remaining schedule will test whether he can continue at anything close to his current rate.For the Oilers, his form offers an encouraging start to the season, particularly when combined with Draisaitl’s contributions, and Edmonton’s 6–5 shootout win over Carolina showed how McDavid’s production can influence close games, with his late tying goal helping the team extend the contest.McDavid’s 31 points are already a historic achievement, regardless of what follows. The Oilers captain is off to one of the most sensational starts to the 2026–27 NHL season and is in elite company with Gretzky, Bossy and Lemieux. Whether he can challenge more scoring records is a question that remains to be answered and depends on his continued production, his health and the Oilers performance over the months ahead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mountain West Connection Football: MW Week 8 Players of the Week
articles.summary: Major upsets are shaking up the conference
articles.body:
Week 8 brought major developments in the Mountain West race, with Wyoming knocking off Air Force, New Mexico handing North Dakota State a costly defeat, Hawai'i rolling past Northern Illinois and Nevada earning a much-needed Homecoming win over San José State.

The weekend featured explosive offensive performances, defensive plays that decided games and a special-teams return that helped swing momentum. With New Mexico and Wyoming strengthening their positions near the top of the conference standings, here are this week's Mountain West Connection Players of the Week.

Offensive Player of the Week: Tyler Hughes, Wyoming

Hughes delivered one of the weekend's most complete performances, leading Wyoming to a 28-14 victory over Air Force in Laramie.

The Cowboys quarterback accounted for 259 total yards and three touchdowns, combining 146 rushing yards with 113 passing yards. He averaged more than 12 yards per carry and finished without a turnover against an Air Force team that entered the game with one of the conference's most dangerous rushing attacks.

Hughes immediately put pressure on the Falcons, opening the scoring with a 68-yard touchdown run. He also threw touchdown passes to Jake Wilson and Samuel Harris before Wyoming added a fourth-quarter rushing score to seal the victory.

The performance was especially important for a Wyoming team that has steadily improved after a difficult start to the season. The Cowboys are now 5-3 overall and 4-1 in conference play, putting themselves firmly in the Mountain West championship conversation.

Hughes earns this week's offensive honor for his ability to hurt Air Force with both his arm and his legs while protecting the football.

Defensive Player of the Week: Austin Brawley, New Mexico

New Mexico's 21-16 victory over North Dakota State featured a defensive play worthy of deciding a major conference matchup.

With the Lobos clinging to a five-point lead in the fourth quarter, defensive back Austin Brawley intercepted North Dakota State quarterback Nathan Hayes and returned the ball 56 yards for a touchdown. The score gave New Mexico the cushion it needed to survive the Bison's late push.

North Dakota State scored again but could not complete the comeback, as New Mexico forced a turnover on downs to secure the win.

Brawley's interception was the defining moment in a game where points were difficult to find. The Lobos also recorded nine tackles for loss, disrupting the Bison's running game and forcing Hayes to shoulder more of the offensive burden through the air.

New Mexico held North Dakota State to 16 points and secured one of its biggest victories of the season. The Lobos improved to 6-1 overall and 3-0 in conference play, while Brawley's pick-six proved to be the difference.

Special Teams Player of the Week: Ky Woods, Nevada

Nevada needed a spark against San José State, and Woods provided it at a crucial moment.

The Wolf Pack led 21-10 in the fourth quarter when the Spartans scored a touchdown to cut the margin to 21-13. Woods responded with a 90-yard kickoff return, setting Nevada up in excellent field position and changing the momentum immediately.

On the very next play, running back Dominic Kelley punched in a four-yard touchdown to restore Nevada's 18-point advantage. The Wolf Pack went on to win 28-13.

Woods' return was the turning point in a game where Nevada's defense had controlled much of the action. The Wolf Pack held San José State to just 70 total yards through the first three quarters and limited the Spartans to 179 yards for the game.

Nevada improved to 3-4 overall and 2-2 in Mountain West play. Woods' return did not go for a touchdown, but its timing and direct impact on the scoreboard make him a deserving special-teams selection.

Micah Alejado, Hawai'i — Offense: Alejado threw for 323 yards and three touchdowns in the Rainbow Warriors' 56-21 victory. His passing performance helped Hawai'i produce its highest-scoring outing of the season.

Luke Duncan, Nevada — Offense: Duncan completed 18 of 29 passes for 178 yards and two touchdowns without an interception in Nevada's 28-13 win over San José State. He delivered career highs in passing yards and touchdown passes.

Wyoming defense — Defense: The Cowboys forced three Air Force fumbles and recorded seven tackles for loss, disrupting a Falcons offense that had been difficult to contain throughout the season.

Dominic Kelley, Nevada — Offense: Kelley carried the ball 24 times for 82 yards and a touchdown, helping Nevada control possession and close out its Homecoming victory.

Week 8 reinforced how quickly the Mountain West race can change. New Mexico strengthened its position at the top with a win over North Dakota State, while Wyoming continued its climb with a statement victory over Air Force. Nevada also showed signs of progress by combining a disciplined defensive performance with timely special-teams execution.

Hughes was the weekend's most productive offensive player, Brawley delivered the defensive play of the week and Woods supplied the momentum-changing return. Meanwhile, Hawai'i's blowout win offered a glimpse of what its offense can accomplish when everything clicks.

With the season entering its final stretch, every conference victory carries added weight. New Mexico and Wyoming have put themselves in strong positions, but Week 8 showed that the race remains far from settled.

articles.title: Inside how the Seahawks defense dominated the Chiefs in Week 7
articles.summary: Inside the numbers of how the Seattle Seahawks defense dominated the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks played complimentary football throughout Sunday's dominant 20-3 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs . The defense especially dominated on primetime in Week 7. It was an elite effort from Mike Macdonald's unit.

The previously 5-0 Chiefs failed to score a touchdown . Per NFL research, that's the first time the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs did not reach the end zone in 153 career starts for the MVP-winning quarterback. That includes postseason appearances.

Former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker has been excellent for the Chiefs this season. The Seahawks totally suffocated him and Andy Reid's running game. Walker, the league-leading rusher, was limited to 36 rushing yards on 14 carries; he averaged just 2.6 yards per attempt, a career-low mark.

Mahomes was 19-of-33 for 165 yards and an interception. No Chiefs pass catcher reached 50 receiving yards.

The Seahawks outgained the Chiefs 410-213, nearly doubling their offensive output. The Seahawks also dominated the time of possession battle 35:51-24:09. That's a credit to both the offense and defense.

An all-around effort from the Seahawks included an elite defensive showing. It was a big-time win for the previously .500 Seahawks, who improved to 4-3 and kickstarted their 2026 season with a statement win.

articles.title: 3 stars from Week 7 for the 49ers: Slim pickings after an off game
articles.summary: We went with three players on the 49ers offense
articles.body:
It was ugly, it was sloppy, and it was bad. But somehow the San Francisco 49ers found themselves with a chance to take the lead with three minutes left in the fourth quarter.

Brock Purdy's second interception of the game killed that hope, and the 49ers suffered their first loss of 2026, falling 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons. Since the Arizona game, it's felt like the 49ers' first loss was coming, but San Francisco staved off defeat with back-to-back one-possession wins before finally succumbing to Atlanta.

With the 49ers taking a 6-1 record into the bye week, these are the three stars from the Week 7 loss:

Let's get it out of the way now: the fumble sucked, and it was the first sign that Sunday might not be the 49ers' day. But on a day where the defense had no standouts, Black's first NFL touchdown and his performance in relief of McCaffrey were good enough to earn the third star, despite the fumble.

With McCaffrey missing most of the first half, it was on Black to step up. And it was a rough start for the rookie. His day opened with a run that lost four yards, a play blown up by Kendal Daniels. He'd get back to zero yards with his next touch, but it wouldn't be until his fifth carry to get his rushing yard total greater than zero.

But then Black would explode from there. The 49ers' third drive would start with an 11-yard catch from George Kittle, but it would be all Black from there. He would move the 49ers into plus territory with a 15-yard run followed by a gain of seven. Black would close the drive with a mostly untouched 30-yard touchdown run to put the 49ers up 14-3.

His next and last impact on the game would be his fumble, but it was an encouraging overall performance with 12 carries for 63 yards and the touchdown in the spell of McCaffrey.

Sunday's loss was such a stinker that half the reason Kittle earned the No. 2 star is that it was a good game on National Tight End Day.

Kittle celebrated the occasion with a game-high eight receptions for 88 yards, responsible for 30 percent of the 49ers' passing offense.

The tight end's day started with a 17-yard reception with the 49ers facing a third-and-4 on the team's second drive of the game. He'd then open the 49ers' next drive with an 11-yard catch to start what would end up being a touchdown-scoring drive.

He'd have a few more short receptions before closing his day with his longest reception, a 21-yard catch, but Kittle fumbled for the 49ers fourth turnover, ending the 49ers slim hopes of a comeback.

Not the best game from the People's Tight End with the turnover, but a good enough performance on a holiday he created (although Kyle Juszczyk being called an "honorary tight end" should be enough to end the gimmick) to earn a star.

Just like with Mike Evans last week against Washington, McCaffrey's knock on Sunday completely hampered the 49ers offense.

It was painfully obvious Sunday was a scheduled McCaffrey game, with the 49ers running back getting six touches of the 49ers' 10-play opening drive. He would take those touches and give the 49ers 69 total yards, ending the drive with a one-yard touchdown run to put San Francisco up 7-0 early.

The 49ers' second drive would start with Purdy connecting with McCaffrey for a five-yard pass with a little under seven minutes left in the first quarter. That would end up being McCaffrey's last touch until the 8:15 mark in the third quarter, with the running back dealing with a thigh injury for most of Sunday.

In the time McCaffrey was off the field, the 49ers offense had three drives that lasted a combined 18 plays for 122 yards, ending in a punt, touchdown, and a fumble lost (on a drive. San Francisco had six drives with McCaffrey on the field, running 47 plays for 281 yards with two touchdowns, but the four others ended in some type of turnover, none at the fault of McCaffrey.

Three drives without McCaffrey averaged six plays for 41 yards, while the six with the running back averaged nearly eight plays for 47 yards. McCaffrey finished Sunday with 13 touches for 100 yards (his second 100-yard game in a row) with the touchdown. Curious just how different Sunday's game could have gone had McCaffrey not missed those two drives. Nonetheless, his performance was easily the best by a 49er in Atlanta.

articles.title: The Penguins saw the old Rickard Rakell on Saturday. They need that guy back
articles.summary: Down 2-1 on Saturday night with the clock ticking away, the Penguins got a signature goal from their three best players on the ice to tie the score. Erik Kar...
articles.body:
Down 2-1 on Saturday night with the clock ticking away, the Penguins got a signature goal from their three best players on the ice to tie the score. Erik Karlsson and Sidney Crosby assisted on Rickard Rakell's late score to tie the game. It was a goal the team desperately needed, and the type of play they haven't made that often early in this year Crosby making a wonderful pass to put a winger in position to score, and then the winger actually scoring.

Unsurprisingly, it was a weight off Rakell's shoulders to tally just his second goal of the season that is now 12 games old.

"It felt so good. The amount of looks I had – first off, in this game – my teammates setting me up for all these chances, it definitely feels good to put one in," Rakell said after the game .

Despite the lack of results, Rakell has been generating chances. He's earned that good feeling and confidence boost from scoring due to all the chances that he's created. Rakell was stopped on a breakaway earlier in the game, and even before that few players in the league have generated as much as Rakell has at 5v5. This data is before the Nashville game, even then, Rakell didn't score a 5v5 goal (since the Penguins had pulled their goalie, it was a 6v5 situation).

Rakell has 30 shots on the year, enough to lead the team by a wide margin (Kris Letang, Ben Kindel and Nick Robertson all have 23 a piece). It's no secret or deep analysis that the Penguins need Rakell to pitch in. Rakell scored 59 goals in the last two full seasons from 2024-25 to 2025-26, in the ballpark with names like Kirill Marchenko, Brock Nelson, Bo Hovat and not too far off Sidney Crosby (62).

Rakell isn't a player the team can afford to have in a slump and expect to get good results. The team's record in first 11 games of the season illustrate that, as did Rakell stepping up to score Saturday in a game the Pens found a way to win in overtime.

The stakes are only raised now that Bryan Rust is on the shelf with injury for at least six weeks, the importance of a player like Rakell only gets magnified when another one of the tried-and-true options is unavailable.

The good news for the Pens may be that Rakell has been generating all those chances, it would be a more difficult conversation to have if this was a player failing to even get in position to score. That hasn't been the problem to this point. It's been about finishing those chances, which can be an area that ebbs and flows for even the most consistent and reliable players over stretches to go hot and cold. For someone as skilled as Rakell, enough chances will lead to goals eventually. Such was what happened on Saturday, getting a prime chance sent his way by Crosby, and then finally breaking through to put the puck in the back of the net.

Rakell was cold early in the season, the Penguins could sure benefit from it if the late goal in their last game was a sign that he is coming out of it and about to start filling the net, as he typically will do over the long haul. The Pittsburgh first line needs it, the power play needs it and the team at large would be in for a big boost if some more red lights behind the goalie follow from the chances Rakell has been generating in front of him.

articles.title: Conte breaks silence amidst reports he could return to Juventus
articles.summary: Several reports have linked Antonio Conte with a return to Juventus and a possible move to Manchester United, with both clubs reportedly considering changes...
articles.body:
Several reports have linked Antonio Conte with a return to Juventus and a possible move to Manchester United, with both clubs reportedly considering changes in the dugout. Conte continues to be associated with Juventus, particularly as Luciano Spalletti faces pressure following a difficult spell at the club.

The Bianconeri have been linked with bringing Conte back on several occasions , and speculation could grow if results fail to improve. The club are also working to ensure they have the right players and managerial leadership to meet their objectives.

John Elkann has shown a willingness to dismiss managers when performances fall below expectations, and there are growing concerns that Spalletti could lose his job in the coming weeks. Some Juventus supporters would welcome Conte's return, although there is no confirmation that the club are preparing to appoint him.

Conte has a strong connection with Juventus, which means his name is likely to feature whenever the club's managerial position comes under scrutiny. However, speculation about a potential reunion does not necessarily mean negotiations are taking place.

(Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Manchester United also linked with Italian coach

Manchester United are another club reportedly considering their options. Michael Carrick could face dismissal before Spalletti, while Conte has reportedly been included on the Red Devils' list of potential managerial candidates.

Some reports have even suggested that Manchester United have held advanced talks with the Italian coach. Conte has now addressed the speculation, making clear that there are no advanced negotiations with any club at present.

Speaking as quoted by Calciomercato , Conte said:

"In light of the rumours published in recent days by various media outlets, both in Italy and abroad, I feel it's appropriate to intervene to clarify matters. My name has been linked to numerous clubs, but at the moment there are no advanced negotiations."After a splendid and successful stint at the helm of Napoli, I will take the time necessary to evaluate how and when to return to coaching. It will be a carefully considered decision, which I will make when I believe the conditions are right."

Conte's comments leave the door open to a future return to management but offer no indication that he is close to accepting either position. Juventus and Manchester United may continue to assess their managerial situations, while Conte intends to take his time before deciding on his next move.

articles.title: ESPN insider takes flamethrower to Miami’s ‘flammable’ defense that’s behind 0-3 start
articles.summary: The Miami Heat are off to a 0-3 start after their 115-110 loss to the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday evening, and an ESPN NBA insider has several specific con...
articles.body:
The Miami Heat are off to a 0-3 start after their 115-110 loss to the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday evening, and an ESPN NBA insider has several specific concerns about their defense. On the latest edition of the Hoop Collective podcast, hosted by Brian Windhorst, NBA insider Tim MacMahon took a "flamethrower" to Miami's "flammable" defense. In his rant, he cited defensive/net ratings to color his criticism.

"The Heat right now are an abysmal defensive team. They're the 3rd worst defensive team in the league. I'm going to read you defensive/net ratings for their starting lineup."

He then read off the defensive/net ratings:

Davion Mitchell: 130.4, -20.6 Klay Thompson: 134.9, -33.5 Andrew Wiggins: 141.5, -39 Giannis Antetokounmpo : 122.9, -28.6 Bam Adebayo: 128.3, -20.5

He continued, saying, "Their starting 5 is flammable right now. — They just aren't that talented out the top 2 guys. There's a pretty massive drop from 2-3 and then it's not a deep team. Klay Thompson's not a starter at this point in his life. Davion Mitchell's never been a starter on a good team. He should be playing 18 MPG or so."

In the Heat's loss against the Hornets, the team gave up 115 points and 16 three-pointers. Antetokounmpo also fouled out. Despite Giannis Antetokounmpo being unable to play in the rest of the game, the Heat almost pulled off a comeback, led by a lineup of Davion Mitchell and Bam Adebayo, with Bobby Portis Jr., Tim Hardaway, and Pelie Larsson. But the team was unable to pull off the comeback and head into Monday's matchup with the Dallas Mavericks winless on the season.

articles.title: Fantasmas en los hoteles de las Series Mundiales
articles.standfirst: Los edificios donde se hospedan como visitantes Milwaukee Brewers y Tampa Bay Rays mantienen amplias leyendas de embrujo
articles.summary: Los edificios donde se hospedan como visitantes Milwaukee Brewers y Tampa Bay Rays mantienen amplias leyendas de embrujo
articles.body: Pocos deportes cultivan la superstición como el béisbol. Hay jugadores que no pisan las líneas, pitchers que repiten el mismo ritual antes de cada salida y bateadores que no se lavan la ropa interior durante una racha ganadora. Es un deporte de 162 partidos a lo largo de la temporada, de muchos kilómetros y pocas horas de descanso, la imaginación muchas veces ve más allá de lo que hay. Las Series Mundiales entre Milwaukee Brewers y Tampa Bay Rays encierra una de las historias de superchería más curiosas: el supuesto encantamiento que tienen los hoteles que suelen albergar a los equipos visitantes, el Pfister, en la ciudad de Wisconsin y el Vinoy Reneissance de San Petersburgo, en Florida, dos edificios centenarios plagados de leyendas urbanas que han circulado de boca en boca durante el siglo. Una experiencia muy común en varios hoteles en Estados Unidos. De hecho, el resplandor de Stephen King surgió de una experiencia 'paranormal' del escritor en uno de ellos... Abierto en 1893 y promovido por el empresario Charles Pfister, el Pfister fue concebido como un símbolo de la pujanza de Milwaukee, la ciudad cervecera de la era dorada. Heredero de una familia de curtidores adinerados, Pfister quiso un hotel que rivalizara con los grandes de la Costa Este, y lo llenó de mármol, maderas nobles y arte. Hoy el hotel presume de albergar una de las mayores colecciones de arte victoriano del mundo en un establecimiento hotelero, algo que forma parte de su identidad. Es el hotel emblemático del centro de Milwaukee, y los equipos visitantes de los Brewers han acostumbrado a alojarse allí. Por sus pasillos han desfilado generaciones de jugadores. Según la tradición local, el espíritu de Pfister, fallecido en 1927, nunca abandonó del todo el edificio que tanto amó. Los relatos que circulan, sin manera de acreditarlo, incluyen luces y televisores que se encienden o apagan solos; puertas que se abren o cierran sin explicación, sombras, pareidolias... así como sensaciones de frío localizadas y la impresión de ser observado. Lo que convierte al Pfister en caso especial es el elemento beisbolero. La leyenda sostiene que el fantasma sería un anfitrión especialmente poco amable con el equipo visitante y que los jugadores rivales de los Brewers, al menos en la versión popular, se llevan peor parte que los locales. De ahí la broma recurrente de que el Pfister es el 'undécimo jugador' de Milwaukee, o una ventaja de campo sobrenatural. Cuentan que algunos peloteros de equipos visitantes han pedido cambiar de habitación o han bromeado con haber dormido mal por culpa del inquilino. En el trasiego de partidos a una y otra ciudad de los finalistas, el Vinoy Renaissance (Marriott) es el hotel de Babe Ruth. Se inauguró en 1925, en pleno boom inmobiliario de Florida, de la mano del empresario Aymer Vinoy Laughner. Fue durante décadas el gran hotel de la costa del Golfo de Florida, un edificio de estilo mediterráneo con vistas a la bahía de Tampa, frecuentado por la alta sociedad y la élite del deporte. También tiene un capítulo beisbolero. St. Petersburgo fue durante años sede de los entrenamientos de primavera de los New York Yankees, y es una tradición muy repetida que figuras como Babe Ruth y Lou Gehrig se alojaron allí. Con el tiempo llegó el declive. El hotel cerró en 1974 y estuvo abandonado durante casi dos décadas, hasta que una gran restauración lo devolvió a la vida a comienzos de los años noventa. Entre los relatos habituales figuran apariciones de personajes de época, ruidos inexplicables en plantas determinadas y la impresión de que ciertos espíritus continúan hoy presos en sus pasillos. Parte del folclore asocia esa presencia espectral a la era dorada del hotel y a los grandes nombres que lo visitaron, con el aura de Ruth como imán narrativo de un edificio que con más de un siglo de vida acumula crujidos, corrientes de aire, instalaciones antiguas y, sobre todo, historias.

articles.title: Elhousine Elazzaoui conquista su tercer título consecutivo de las Golden Trail World Series
articles.standfirst: El corredor de NNormal se impone en la Gran Final de Muju Trail, en Corea del Sur, y se convierte en el corredor más laureado de la historia del circuito
articles.summary: El corredor de NNormal se impone en la Gran Final de Muju Trail, en Corea del Sur, y se convierte en el corredor más laureado de la historia del circuito
articles.body: El corredor de NNormal Elhousine Elazzaoui ha vuelto a hacer historia en el trail running. El atleta marroquí se ha proclamado campeón de las Golden Trail World Series (GTWS) por tercera temporada consecutiva tras imponerse en la Gran Final de Muju Trail, en Corea del Sur. Una victoria que confirma su dominio en el circuito internacional y lo sitúa como el atleta con más títulos en la historia de la competición. Elazzaoui cerró la temporada de la mejor manera posible: ganando la última carrera del calendario en un desenlace que ha mantenido la lucha por el título abierta hasta el final. Con este resultado, suma cuatro victorias en las GTWS 2026, tras imponerse también en Zegama-Aizkorri, Ledro Sky Trentino y Pitz Alpine Glacier Trail. La Gran Final de Muju Trail planteó un desafío exigente: 28,65 kilómetros y 2.313 metros de desnivel positivo, con lluvia, terreno técnico y descensos que requerían precisión y confianza. El marroquí llegaba a Corea del Sur en tercera posición de la clasificación general, obligado a ganar para mantener sus opciones de conquistar un nuevo título. Desde los primeros kilómetros, Elazzaoui dejó claras sus intenciones. Tras un inicio marcado por la lucha entre los principales aspirantes al título, lanzó un ataque decisivo durante la primera ascensión. Alrededor del kilómetro 6,5, ya había abierto una ventaja aproximada de un minuto sobre sus perseguidores. Los descensos técnicos, con escalones, rocas y hojas mojadas, pusieron a prueba la capacidad de los corredores para mantener el ritmo y controlar cada apoyo. Elazzaoui encontró en este terreno una oportunidad para ampliar su ventaja y consolidar su posición al frente de la carrera. "Sabía que tenía que ganar esta carrera si quería luchar por el título, así que salí dispuesto a darlo todo. Las condiciones eran difíciles y tuve que mantener la concentración en todo momento. Ganar mi tercer título consecutivo es algo muy especial para mí. Estoy muy contento con la temporada que hemos hecho y con poder terminarla así", explica Elazzaoui, el nómada del desierto que conquista montañas. A medida que avanzaban los kilómetros, el atleta de NNormal fue aumentando la distancia respecto a sus rivales. En la parte final, mientras la lucha por las posiciones de podio se intensificaba, el marroquí mantuvo el control y cruzó la línea de meta en 2:49:14, con 43 segundos de ventaja sobre Patrick Kipngeno. Timothy Kibett completó el podio. La victoria en Muju no solo supuso el cuarto triunfo de Elazzaoui en la temporada, sino también la pieza definitiva para completar una nueva conquista de las Golden Trail World Series. La clasificación general llegó a la última prueba con todo por decidir. Aunque Elazzaoui partía desde la tercera posición, su victoria en la Gran Final le permitió remontar hasta lo más alto de la clasificación, con un total de 1.130 puntos. Patrick Kipngeno terminó segundo, con 1.128 puntos, mientras que Philemon Kiriago cerró la temporada en tercera posición, con 1.075. La diferencia de solo dos puntos entre los dos primeros refleja la intensidad de una temporada en la que cada carrera y cada segmento han tenido un papel decisivo. Con este resultado, Elhousine Elazzaoui logra su tercer título consecutivo de las Golden Trail World Series, después de sus triunfos en 2024 y 2025. Una trayectoria que consolida al corredor de NNormal entre las grandes figuras del trail running internacional y que añade un nuevo capítulo a su historia en el circuito.

articles.summary: Explore how Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, built an $800 million empire through WWE, Hollywood movies, and lucrative business ventures while balancing family life with Lauren Hashian.
articles.body: Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, has built a career that includes professional wrestling, blockbuster movies, TV production and entrepreneurship, and he started his career in WWE, where his charm and unique persona made him a household name before transitioning successfully into Hollywood. His professional portfolio today includes acting, producing, consumer brands and leadership roles in sports entertainment.Johnson’s estimated net worth is $800 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. His personal wealth and private businesses can fluctuate in value, and his wealth is not just from one stream of income but a mix of earnings from entertainment, business ventures, brand partnerships and investments.How Dwayne Johnson built his multi million fortuneJohnson’s financial journey began in professional wrestling, and he joined WWE in 1996 and performed as Rocky Maivia before developing The Rock persona that helped establish him as one of wrestling's biggest attractions. He was a standout personality in WWE’s Attitude Era because he could mix athletic performances, humour and memorable promos.Wrestling gave him his public profile, but Johnson had ambitions outside of the ring. His foray into acting also exposed him to another audience and a broader spectrum of professional possibilities. His first roles, such as The Scorpion King helped him establish his screen career, and later roles in big franchises increased his international recognition.Johnson's net worth is estimated to be around $800 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. The estimate includes the possible value of his business interests and should not be confused with his cash on hand.How The Rock expanded beyond wrestling and HollywoodJohnson’s business interests include entertainment production, beverages, sports and lifestyle products. These enterprises allow him to leverage his public profile in markets that live outside the release of individual films.And that’s where Seven Bucks Productions comes in. Johnson and businesswoman Dany Garcia co-founded the company in 2012, which develops and produces film, television and digital entertainment. It has worked on titles including Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle, Jumanji: The Next Level, Hobbs & Shaw and Red Notice. The company employs Johnson both in front of and behind the camera.Another high-profile venture is Tequila Teremana, which launched in 2020. The brand is in the competitive spirits market and adds a consumer product to Johnson’s portfolio. Its commercial success and any private ownership valuations can influence estimates of his overall wealth, but the value of a business is not the same as cash that is immediately available to its owners.How Dwayne Johnson balances business success and family lifeJohnson’s family life is a big part of his public persona, particularly his wife, Lauren Hashian. Singer, songwriter and music producer, Hashian has carved out her own creative career while sharing family life with one of the most recognizable faces in the entertainment industry.The pair first crossed paths in 2006 while Johnson was shooting The Game Plan. Their relationship developed over the years and they married in Hawaii on 18 August 2019. Together they have two daughters, Jasmine and Tiana. Johnson also has one older daughter, Simone, with ex-wife Dany Garcia. Simone has also been involved in professional wrestling, wrestling for WWE under the name Ava.Hashian's music work provides the couple with interests away from Johnson's film and business commitments. While she is often seen with him at public events, her identity is not just that of a famous actor's wife. Her own professional background includes songwriting and music work.Johnson and Garcia have also kept up a working relationship since their divorce. They continued to work together at Seven Bucks Productions, showing how personal and professional relationships can grow over time. Garcia still plays a major role as a business partner in Johnson’s entertainment career.Dwayne Johnson's luxury properties and lifestyleAnother aspect of Johnson’s lifestyle that is easy to see is real estate. He has been reported to own large properties in the U.S. over the years, including homes in California and an estate in Georgia. Celebrity property holdings, however, can fluctuate. Previous purchases or listings should not be considered definitive proof of current ownership.One much-publicized case involved a 2019 purchase of a property in Powder Springs, Georgia. The property coverage described the estate as a large equestrian estate with extensive grounds and a large residence. Later reports suggested the property was on the market. This is an example of why real estate information should be checked against the date of a report before a property is described as being in someone's current portfolio.Johnson was also reported to have bought a Beverly Park estate in California in 2021. This is a neighbourhood of celebrity residents and high-priced homes. While the reported price of the property drew attention to the purchase, the value of a home on the market is not always indicative of the profit or cash on hand to the owner.Luxury homes can be for a number of reasons, including privacy, family living and long-term asset ownership. But the price paid for a property is not the only factor deciding its current worth, and ownership details can change. A reliable account of Johnson’s real estate holdings should distinguish between confirmed transactions and properties he might have sold or no longer owns.What makes The Rock's empire different?What’s notable about Johnson’s career is how it has combined several routes to commercial success. Wrestling built his persona and fan base, Hollywood extended his reach; production gave him a role in developing content; and consumer brands created opportunities outside of entertainment contracts.Johnson’s net worth is estimated at $800 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth, but that number should be taken as an estimate that is partly influenced by the valuation of his business interests. articles.body: The Philadelphia Flyers have received a major blow as they lose $25.5 million veteran defenseman to two weeks after suffering an injury. articles.body: El fútbol colombiano vuelve a tener protagonismo en los galardones más prestigiosos del planeta. En la ceremonia del Balón de Oro 2026, celebrada en el London Palladium Theatre de Londres, se confirmó que Luis Díaz finalizó en la posición 24 de las votaciones mundiales. El extremo guajiro, consolidado como una de las máximas figuras del Bayern Múnich y de la Selección Colombia, se metió una vez más dentro del selecto grupo de los 30 mejores jugadores del mundo, ratificando su regularidad en el balompié de máxima exigencia europea. El reconocimiento al exjugador del Liverpool llega tras una campaña sobresaliente (2025/26) con el conjunto bávaro en su primera etapa en Alemania. Durante este periodo, Lucho acumuló números de auténtico peso pesado: Partidos jugados: 51 Goles anotados: 26 Asistencias repartidas: 23 Títulos conquistados: 3 trofeos con el Bayern Múnich. Gracias a estas estadísticas, el extremo se perfilaba fuertemente previo a las citas mundialistas para escalar aún más alto en el ranking de la revista France Football. Sin embargo, a pesar de su buen andar en clubes, el desempeño de la Selección Colombia en el Mundial de 2026 —donde el equipo nacional compitió pero no logró alcanzar las instancias definitivas— terminó pesando en la sumatoria final de votos. A su arribo a territorio inglés, el atacante guajiro acaparó los focos de la prensa internacional y respondió con total franqueza sobre quién es su principal candidato para levantar el prestigioso galardón que premia al mejor jugador del planeta. Sin titubeos ni rodeos, ‘Lucho’ dejó claro su respaldo hacia uno de sus compañeros en el conjunto bávaro: “¿Mi favorito? Harry, Harry siempre”, apuntó el colombiano, destacando la gran temporada del delantero británico, quien se perfila como uno de los máximos contendientes de la ceremonia. Con esta casilla número 24, Luis Díaz logró superar en las votaciones a reconocidas figuras del panorama internacional como Marquinhos (25°), Dayot Upamecano (26°), Bruno Fernandes (27°) y William Saliba (29°). Esta marca representa la segunda ocasión en la que el colombiano logra meterse en el prestigioso top 30 del Balón de Oro, luego de haber ocupado la decimoséptima posición en la edición del año 2022. A sus 29 años, Luis Díaz continúa escribiendo páginas doradas para el deporte colombiano, demostrando que su velocidad, desequilibrio y cuota goleadora siguen vigentes en la élite del fútbol mundial.

articles.title: ESPN tracking highlights Buccaneers' dominant offensive line
articles.summary: ESPN reports the Buccaneers gained an NFL season-high 171 rushing yards before contact in their 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers rushed for 258 yards in Sunday's 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers , but ESPN's tracking data shows just how much of that production started with the offensive line.

According to ESPN Insights , Tampa Bay gained 171 rushing yards before contact, the highest single-game total by any NFL team this season. The Buccaneers also called designed runs on 81% of their offensive plays, finishing with 49 rushing attempts and three touchdowns.

That means approximately 66% of Tampa Bay's rushing yards came before defenders made contact with the ball carrier. The offensive line consistently created running lanes, allowing Bucky Irving, Kenneth Gainwell, and Sean Tucker to build momentum before they met Carolina's defense.

Irving finished with 106 yards and two touchdowns on 24 carries, while Gainwell added 88 yards on 14 attempts. Tucker contributed 52 yards, including a 46-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. The three running backs combined for 246 rushing yards and all three of Tampa Bay's rushing touchdowns.

The blocking also helped the Buccaneers produce 17 rushing first downs, the third-most allowed in a single game in Panthers franchise history. Tampa Bay's 49 rushing attempts tied the most Carolina has ever surrendered in a game, a mark previously set against San Francisco in 1997.

Offensive coordinator Zach Robinson deserves credit for recognizing the advantage and continuing to exploit it. With Baker Mayfield returning from a thumb injury and right tackle Luke Goedeke sidelined, Tampa Bay had little reason to force the pass. Mayfield attempted just 11 passes and avoided a sack.

The performance doesn't mean Tampa Bay's offensive-line problems have disappeared. Carolina struggled to defend the run, and the Buccaneers will face tougher defensive fronts moving forward. However, generating 171 yards before contact shows how effectively the offensive line executed Sunday, giving Tampa Bay a foundation to build on heading into its Week 8 matchup against Atlanta.

articles.title: Spurs release full 2026-27 TV schedule, including 22 free games on CWSA
articles.summary: The Spurs announced their 2026-27 broadcast schedule, featuring 65 streamed games on DAZN and 22 free, over-the-air broadcasts on CWSA.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs fans now have a clearer picture of where to watch Victor Wembanyama and company this season, including dozens of locally streamed games and 22 games available for free over the air.

The Spurs announced their 2026-27 broadcast schedule Monday. It features 65 regular-season games available locally on the paid sports streaming service DAZN and 22 games airing for free on CWSA (CW 35) .

The team's first CWSA broadcast is Tuesday, when the Spurs visit the Sacramento Kings.

The free broadcasts include two international games between the Spurs and the New Orleans Pelicans - one in Paris on Jan. 14, the other in Manchester, England, three days later - as well as a March 19 matchup against the Dallas Mavericks at the Frost Bank Center.

Fans in Austin, Corpus Christi and the Rio Grande Valley will have access to selected over-the-air broadcasts through local television partners.

DAZN's 65-game lineup includes a Nov. 29 matchup against the Boston Celtics and a March 5 Texas showdown against the Houston Rockets. More games could be added, depending on how the Spurs fare in the NBA Cup, an in-season tournament that starts Oct. 30 and runs through Dec. 11.

DAZN costs $19.99 per month or $119.99 for a season pass and is available throughout the Spurs' home broadcast market, which encompasses Central, South and West Texas. Fans can stream games through the DAZN app on smart TVs, smartphones, tablets and other connected devices.

Nationally, 34 Spurs games will air across NBC, Peacock, Amazon Prime Video, ABC and ESPN, with five additional games on NBA TV.

Former Spurs star Sean Elliott returns for his 26th season as lead television analyst alongside play-by-play announcer Jacob Tobey, who is entering his third season.

All Spurs games will air on WOAI 1200-AM with Dan Weiss, while Paul Castro will provide Spanish-language broadcasts on KXTN 1350-AM.

Fans can find the complete broadcast schedule and viewing options at Spurs.com/Watch or through the official Spurs mobile app.

The 39-year-old has been in good spirits, giving a welcome message to the 16 clubs participating, then laughing as he realized a translator was waiting to put his lengthy comments in Spanish into English as the teenagers stood in the wind and rain of Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

Messi was in Europe last week, accepting the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, a top prestegious award in Spain, in Oviedo. But he returned to the Americas and came into Inter Miami's 2-0 loss to the New York Red Bulls in the 56th minute.

articles.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander wasn't fighting back tears. He was crying. And Mark Daigneault didn't mince words.

"We're not doing great," the Thunder coach said.

It just looks further away than it did 48 hours ago.

articles.title: Morgan Scalley gives update on Kelvin Obot ahead of Cincinnati showdown
articles.summary: Obot missed Utah's win vs. Houston after being injured early in win at Colorado.
articles.body:
Five-star freshman offensive lineman Kelvin Obot had worked his way into the starting lineup and was playing at a pretty high level at right guard for Utah — especially in pass blocking.

Obot played 244 snaps over the first seven games of the season, earning a starting nod as the Utes opened conference play at Iowa State.

The five-star from Fruitland, Idaho, has the unique chance to be coached by his high school head coach, Jordan Gross, who is now in charge of Utah's offensive line.

"Kelvin's just had phenomenal progress since the day he got here," Gross said. "Obviously I've known him for a long time and I'm actually surprised with how well he's done. I knew he'd do really well, but I thought it might take a little bit longer. It's just a tough step from high school to being a starter at this level.

"He's a sponge for knowledge. He loves watching film. He loves asking the veteran guys any information he can get. He hunts me down constantly to watch extra tape and study more."

Obot remained the starter for the next two games, but suffered an injury early in the Utes' win against Colorado, with senior Solatoa Moea'i filling in at left guard. Obot was ruled out for Saturday's game against Houston, and the assumption was that Moea'i would start at left guard against Houston, but Moea'i did not play. Instead it was Roger Alderman at left guard, who played a good game.

Alderman could see at least a few more starts this season.

On Monday, Utah coach Morgan Scalley gave an update on the status of Obot.

"No timetable. He's not out for the season, but we're still getting a second opinion on things and just to give him options as to what he wants to do," Scalley said. "There is a possibility that he could be done for the season depending on what that opinion comes back as. But for right now, there's still a possibility he plays.

If Obot is out for an extended period of time, does Utah go with the starting lineup of Zereoue Willams, Roger Alderman, Alex Harrison, Keith Olson and Cedric Jefferson?

The right side of Utah's line — especially Jefferson — struggled a bit during the first half, but after some adjustments, turned in a better second-half performance.

"Just better communication. Better communication from the offensive line, the tight ends," Scalley said of the adjustments that led to success. "There were a couple times in the first half where we flipped protections where we shouldn't have, and that's going to cause free hitters to come. Much better communication in the second half.

"That's another group, man, right there that watch that film and watch them finish, watch them push our running backs forward, our wide receivers forward, run down the field. I love that crew. The O-block is doing a really nice job."

Utah's offensive line, likely sans Obot, will have another challenge on their hands against Cincinnati's defensive front. The Bearcats are allowing 145 rushing yards per game (No. 76 in the country), but Cincinnati will likely follow the leads of Colorado and Houston in selling out to stop running back Wayshawn Parker.

Against Houston, Parker had 47 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries, only eclipsing 10 yards on one rush — an 18-yard rush in the fourth quarter.

The focus on stopping Parker meant that quarterback Devon Dampier had lanes to run, so Utah went that route to great success as Dampier racked up 150 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

"A lot of it was they wanted to crash down. They were like, 'OK, Wayshawn's not going to beat us,'" Scalley said. "What you have to do is maybe some different things in terms of disguising how you're going to run the ball, some more gap scheme stuff that's not necessarily a QB pull or an option read.

"But they were basically saying, we want him to pull it. We want him to pitch it. Devon was doing a really good job of making that work."

articles.title: Bucks' Taylor Jenkins gives thoughts on LeBron James joining the 76ers
articles.summary: Milwaukee Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins gives his thoughts on LeBron James joining the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers were the big winners of the offseason with the big addition of LeBron James in free agency. The Sixers were able to land James following a weeks long negotiation period and were able to add the future Hall of Famer alongside Jaylen Brown to join Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and VJ Edgecombe to make a run at the title.

James is such a smart basketball player and understands what it takes to succeed in this league as evidenced by his four championships, four finals MVP awards, and four regular season MVP awards along with countless other records. He has won and been successful his entire career no matter where he's been. There's always an adjustment period, but it's always followed by success.

Before the Sixers knocked off the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday at the Xfinity Mobile Arena, Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins gave his thoughts on James with Philadelphia.

"I mean, just elite basketball player on both sides of the floor," Jenkins said of James. "I think just the connectivity, him, the rest of his teammates are fostering right now early in the season. The way that they're playing, they're outletting the ball, they're kicking it ahead. They're one of the faster-paced teams. Yes, they play in isolations, but then they find their teammates."

To Jenkins' point, superstars are going to have isolation moments. It happens, but the Sixers have been moving the ball and getting everybody involved. The entire starting lineup is averaging 3-plus assists through the first four games of the season and everybody is getting their shots and touches.

"I mean, you look at the shot distribution," Jenkins added. "It's not just one guy shooting all the shots and everyone standing around. Obviously, all their starters in double-digit field goal attempts. The assists. I think they got multiple guys that have three-plus right now. So the selflessness right there. I think it's a trickle-down effect and it just permeates throughout the entire roster. So, that's obviously been one of LeBron's greatest strengths his entire career is just how he can ignite offenses."

With so much talent up and down the roster, the Sixers will be tough to stop once they get chemistry down. The defensive effort has been ahead of their offense to start the season, but Philadelphia is looking to figure all of that out. Jenkins sees it from afar with the Bucks as he knows what James can do.

"On the ball, off the ball, his willingness to run without the ball just becomes infectious," Milwaukee's coach finished. "You see him be bringing the ball right now, and obviously two really top-flight, you know, young guards as well. You got Jaylen Brown, who can also initiate an offense too. So all five of those guys, any given moment, knowing that if they're pushing the charge, everyone's kind of running with them, it's going to be pretty lethal to stop."

articles.title: Texas State football grades: Defense surged as offense lulls in win over Utah State
articles.summary: Texas State football ground out a 20-17 win Saturday over Utah State. Here are the grades from the Bobcats' performance.
articles.body:
Texas State football overcame a slow start Saturday to defeat Utah State 20-17. The Bobcats are over .500 for the first time this season as they prepare for a two-game road stretch.

Texas State's (4-3, 2-1 Pac-12) revamped defense has begun to come together, and its special teams proved key in Saturday's win. Consistency could take the program to the next level, and upcoming opponent Boise State (6-1, 3-0) is one of the nation's most stable Group of Six teams.

But before the Bobcats travel to play the Broncos, here are the grades from Texas State's performance vs. Utah State:

This game goes down as one of the worst offensive days in head coach GJ Kinne's tenure with Texas State. The Aggies had an excellent game plan, limiting the Bobcats' run game to 2.7 yards per carry and forcing them to win through the air. Texas State finished with 250 total yards, its lowest of the season

Utah State pressured Texas State quarterback Brad Jackson, and he struggled to punish the blitz. Jackson made the right read on a few instances, missing his target on potentially explosive plays. He threw for 167 yards on 27-of-37 passing. He was sacked four times.

When Texas State struggles to run the ball, the offense tends to stagnate; the third quarter at San Diego State, when they averaged 2.5 yards per carry, is another example.

Texas State defensive coordinator Will Windham said in the offseason it would take time for things to gel. The unit hasn't been perfect, but the defense has improved each week. It held Utah State to 17 points while ending nearly a half-dozen drives before they covered more than 10 yards.

Defensive back Trez Moore had a career night, disrupting plays, breaking up a pass and nearly nabbing an interception. Linebacker Treylin Payne led the team in tackles (nine) and is returning to form after joining the roster late in the summer. Defensive lineman Chancellor Owens is the bedrock against the run game, holding Utah State to 2.3 yards per carry.

Texas State recorded one sack. The lack of pressure from the edge rushers remains somewhat of an issue.

Special teams had some highs and lows. On one hand, Texas State would've lost without Jacob Bonilla's two field goals and running back Jaylen Jenkins' 100-yard kick return touchdown. Bonilla, in particular, showed great mental fortitude after missing a 49-yard attempt.

The punting still hasn't been up to snuff. Tom Flintoff averaged 36 yards on five attempts. He gave Utah State two short fields in the first quarter on 34- and 35-yard punts. Flintoff improved in the following quarters, recording two punts over 40 yards and forcing one drive to start at the 12.

Texas State has struggled in the third quarter this season, and Kinne acknowledges this. Maybe it was receiving the kickoff out of halftime or some other coaching strategy, but the Bobcats opened the third against the Aggies with a 12-play, 79-yard touchdown drive.

Kinne's preached resilience in recent weeks, and Texas State showed it against Utah State. It hadn't won a game in which it trailed at halftime since 2024 against South Alabama. Down 9-7, the Bobcats regrouped and proved they didn't need their explosive offense to beat the Aggies, who were just 4-for-14 on third down.

articles.title: Inside Canelo’s record after losses and what it means for Christian Mbilli fight
articles.summary: Here's a breakdown of Canelo Alvarez’s losses and the result of each fight he’s been in after.
articles.body:
A loss can make or break a fighter. They can either step up and improve, or falter and succumb to the pressure. While he hasn't lost many fights, Canelo Alvarez has proven he can step up following setbacks.

Canelo has lost three fights in his career. Each against great fighters spanning different phases of his career: Floyd Mayweather, Dmitry Bivol, and Terence Crawford.

The Mexican fighter recovered following losses against Mayweather and Bivol. Fans will now have to wait and see how Canelo will do a year after losing to Crawford. He faces Christian Mbilli on Halloween for the WBC super middleweight title.

Here's a breakdown of Canelo's losses, and perhaps more relevant to the Mbilli fight, what happened in his return.

Sept. 14, 2013: lost to Floyd Mayweather via majority decision

Next fight: def. Alfredo Angulo via TKO on March 8, 2014

Canelo was just 23 when he fought Floyd Mayweather in 2013.

Canelo couldn't cut off the ring against the defensive-minded Mayweather, who at 36 was incredibly still in an extended prime. Mayweather actually showcased his offense, landing 232 of 505 punches (46%), while Canelo landed 117 of 526 (22%). Mayweather landed 139 jabs and won via majority decision.

The fight was considered an eye-opener for Canelo. It also started a run we may never see again. Canelo went 15-0-1 after the Mayweather fight, winning gold across multiple divisions.

Canelo's next fight was a catchweight bout against Alfredo Angulo in March. It was a lopsided battle, with Canelo earning a tenth-round stoppage win. He landed 64% of his power punches.

May 7, 2022: lost to Dmitry Bivol via unanimous decision

Next fight: def. Gennady Golovkin via unanimous decision on Sept. 17, 2022

Canelo competed at light heavyweight in 2019, easily dispatching Sergey Kovalev. After, the weight-jumping Canelo returned to super middleweight and became undisputed in the division by beating Caleb Plant. From there, it was believed that whatever Canelo wanted, Canelo got. That included a return to light heavyweight against Dmitry Bivol.

The mighty Canelo flew too close to the sun against Bivol.

Bivol threw an average of 59 punches per round, landing 13. He landed 152 of 710 strikes (21.4%) compared to just 84 of 495 (17%) for Canelo, a career-low.

Canelo wanted to avenge the loss, but managed to get a trilogy fight against Gennadiy Golovkin. While a few years too late, there was still interest. Canelo controlled the fight, landing 130 of 487 strikes (26.7%) compared to 120 of 521 (23%) for GGG. While Golovkin landed 74 jabs, Canelo landed 85 power punches. Canelo won via unanimous decision.

Sept. 13, 2025: lost to Terence Crawford via unanimous decision

Next fight: TBD vs. Christian Mbilli on Oct. 31, 2026

Canelo was on a six-fight win streak after losing against Bivol. He once again became undisputed at super middleweight while beating fighters from Jermell Charlo to William Scull. Looking for a challenge, Canelo and welterweight great Terence Crawford agreed to a super fight in September 2025.

Crawford used a jab and hook to push Canelo back. Crawford had the edge, and it was in the later rounds that he brought Canelo to school. He landed a hook that clipped Canelo's chin and showcased his speed throughout the fight. Crawford landed 115 of 534 punches (21.5%) and Canelo landed 99 of 338 (29.3%).

Crawford retired after the fight. As for Canelo? We wait to see what happens against Christian Mbilli.

articles.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen provides little information on Tyler Warren; Alec Pierce remains on IR
articles.summary: Colts have nearly a half-dozen starters injured heading into Week 8. Here's what head coach Shane Steichen said Monday about the team's injured list
articles.body:
Colts tight end Tyler Warren has been "progressing really well" as he works his way back from a groin injury suffered in practice Oct. 16, according to coach Shane Steichen but he was non-committal on whether Warren would practice for the first time in nearly two weeks.

Warren was a game-time decision for the Colts ' eventual 26-20 loss to Tennessee but didn't play and didn't practice or play last week.

"I don't know yet," Steichen said Monday in regards to Warren's prospects of practicing this week. "But we'll see how the week goes."

Indianapolis Colts photos vs Minnesota Vikings in NFL Week 7

Despite two missed games, Warren still leads Indianapolis' anemic offense with 30 catches, one more than veteran wideout Keenan Allen (29). Warren is third on the team in targets (36) and yards (213). He also remains the only Colt with multiple receiving touchdowns (two).

Pierce remains on injured reserve due to his surgically repaired left heel – he could've returned to practice this past week after having missed four games but, along with veteran defensive end Micheal Clemons (toe), Steichen said Monday that neither player was likely to return to practice this week ahead of the team's Week 8 visit to Jacksonville.

The Colts were without starting All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner on Sunday due to a left calf injury he suffered in Week 6 and then lost two more of its secondary due to injury in the game against the Vikings .

Nickel cornerback Justin Walley missed Wednesday's practice last week and was limited Thursday and Friday with a knee injury, but he played into Sunday's second half before leaving the game with a knee injury. The team also lost rotational corner and key special-teamer Cam Taylor-Britt to a groin injury, leaving Indianapolis without three of its top four corners.

Steichen said he was uncertain of that group's status for practice this week. "We're working through that," the head coach said Monday.

The Colts' rookie rotational linebackers CJ Allen (ankle) and Bryce Boettcher (groin) were ruled inactive for Sunday's game. The Colts also are still without starting edge rusher Arden Key , who suffered a hamstring injury in Week 4 before being placed on IR. The earliest Key can return to practice will be in preparation for the team's Week 9 home game against the Cowboys.

articles.title: Instant Takeaways from the Vikings' Week 7 win over the Colts
articles.summary: We have some instant takeaways to share from the Vikings' Week 7 win.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings came back from their Bye Week well rested and ready for what was expected to be a tough Indianapolis Colts team. The game started out rough as they struggled in the first half, even on the first drive, but they made adjustments and shut out the Colts in the second half.

The big star of the game was the defense, as Brian Flores had his guys creating chaos and then some. They never let Daniel Jones have time to think, and they struggled with Jonathan Taylor in the first quarter. The Vikings' offense struggled at times, especially establishing the run, but Kyler Murray made some impressive throws throughout. The offense still has some work to do, but as long as the defense plays like this, they will have plenty of time to make adjustments.

Here are our instant takeaways from the Vikings' interesting win in Week 7.

Kyler Murray has not had the easiest go of things during the start of his tenure as starter of the Minnesota Vikings. He has found small bits of rhythm here and there, but he has shown promise nonetheless. Vikings fans have to be patient; it won't be easy, but he can be what Sam Darnold was eventually. This is the best system, with the best line, and the best skill players he has been around, so it will take some adjusting.

Blake Cashman had one of the best games I have ever watched in terms of production and what he put on film. All season long he has continued to make plays and is on pace for career highs in several areas. I was skeptical of Harrison Smith as a Hall of Famer; I shouldn't have been. The company he now has after his 40th interception is among the best safeties and defenders in the history of the game. His returning may not have made the most sense, but it is a move that is now paying dividends for the Vikings and then some.
