articles.title: Maple Leafs’ Easton Cowan impresses Gavin McKenna with his development in Toronto
articles.summary: Matching up against opponents' top lines helps Easton Cowan create offensive opportunities.
articles.body:
Toronto Maple Leafs forward Easton Cowan has impressed teammate Gavin McKenna with his development and ability to handle difficult matchups. The young forward has earned greater responsibility while contributing offensively and maintaining his defensive discipline.

Speaking to reporters Monday morning ahead of Toronto's game against the Calgary Flames, McKenna praised Cowan's progress. He highlighted the challenge of facing opposing teams' top lines while continuing to produce points.

" For him to go against first lines every night while still putting up points and not getting caught out defensively is very impressive," McKenna said.

"The jump he's made from last year has been unbelievable to watch," he added.

So far Cowan has registered 12 points in 13 games, which includes 5 goals while playing just over 15 minutes. If we compare this number to his performance last season, he is just 6 goals and 17 points short.

McKenna also pointed to Cowan's growing confidence as an important part of his development. The two players share a close friendship, making Cowan's progress particularly rewarding for McKenna.

"He's playing with a lot of confidence right now, and how could you not when you're playing like that?" McKenna said. "He's one of my best buddies, so it's great to see."

Easton Cowan embraces defensive responsibility

Cowan has also welcomed the challenge of matching up against opposing teams' leading forwards. Rather than viewing those assignments as a burden, the Maple Leafs forward sees them as an opportunity to create offense through responsible defensive play.

"I like playing against other teams' top lines," Cowan said. "It's fun. It brings intensity, and if you have good defense, it can lead to offense."

His approach reflects the importance of playing a complete game at the NHL level. Limiting dangerous chances while winning puck battles can create opportunities for Toronto to transition quickly.

"So I'm just trying to be simple, get pucks, and let the defense lead to offense," Cowan explained. "That's kind of what I've been living by, so just trying to keep that going."

For Toronto, Cowan's development offers encouraging signs. His ability to contribute at both ends could make him an increasingly valuable part of the team's long-term plans.

McKenna's praise also highlights the confidence Cowan has earned from those around him. If he maintains this balance, he could continue growing into a dependable contributor for the Maple Leafs.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns look for an answer to their third-quarter struggles in SEC play
articles.summary: Despite taking leads into the halftime intermission of all four of its SEC games, the Longhorns are 2-2 in their conference games. Texas has been outscored b...
articles.body:
During SEC play, Texas football often found itself halfway home to a conference conquest.

But as most football fans know, a game on the collegiate level lasts for 60 minutes so what the scoreboard says while the home team's band is performing at halftime isn't permanent. Those numbers are simply a placeholder.

That has proven to be the case for Texas (5-2, 2-2 SEC). Despite taking leads into the halftime intermission of all four of its SEC games, the Longhorns have lost twice and had their two wins come down to a last-second heave into the end zone.

Why haven't all of these halftime leads translated into wins? Well, let's start with what is happening to the UT offense in the third quarter.

Over its four SEC games, Texas has been outscored by a 31-3 margin in the third quarter with those three points coming Sept. 26 at Tennessee . The Longhorns have averaged 0.8 yards over 30 third-quarter rushes - five of which were sacks - while UT quarterback Arch Manning has gone 10-of-20 for 103 yards. Texas had gained six first downs in those third quarters, punted 10 times and committed one turnover.

Are those numbers out of the norm? Overall, the Longhorns are scoring 25.5 points per game in conference play. Texas is averaging 3.5 yards over its 140 rushes - 15 of which are sacks - while Manning had thrown for 846 yards while completing 65 of his 100 passes. Mac Chiumento has punted just 13 times outside of the third quarter.

"We've just got to do our 1-11. If one thing goes wrong, you can see what happens out there," tight end Michael Masunas said.

What adjustments are the Texas Longhorns making at halftime?

The Longhorns' second-half struggles might lead one to wonder what's happening in the Texas locker room during halftime. So what is happening in the Texas locker room during halftime?

Earlier this month, NFL quarterback Aaron Rodgers told reporters that halftime breaks for football players may not be what people envision . Sure, some adjustments are made and meetings are held. For the most part, though, players use the time to catch their breaths.

On Monday, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian was asked about his halftime routine. Sarkisian shared that the staff huddles for a quick meeting where he points out a few things that are going well and a few things that need to change. Some adjustments are made, some film is reviewed and some plays are drawn up for the second half. The coaches will also chat with players.

Sarkisian conceded that this routine may not be currently working for the Longhorns. That may lead to some adjustment to the way that Texas makes its halftime adjustments.

"I'm not opposed to making subtle tweaks and changes to what we do at halftime," Sarkisian said. "There'll be probably a couple things we do different this Saturday night at halftime to get ourselves ready to go, ready to play to start the second half."

On Saturday, the 11th-ranked team in the Associated Press poll will play its third straight home game when Mississippi State (4-3, 2-3) comes to town. In SEC play, the Bulldogs have been outscored in the third quarter in four of their five conference games. So that may give the Longhorns a chance to get right when it comes to their third-quarter issues.

"It's frustrating. We'll get it right, though," Manning said.
